html:
In 612 BCE an alliance of Babylonians and Medes besieged and sacked Nineveh, the capital of Assyria, on the Tigris opposite today's Mosul. It was the death blow to the Assyrian Empire.

Assyria had ruled from Egypt to Iran, but after the death of Ashurbanipal it was torn by civil war. Babylon rose in revolt under Nabopolassar, and the Medes joined him. After a siege of about three months the city fell and was burned. The last Assyrian forces were beaten at Harran and Carchemish over the next years.

The Hebrew prophet Nahum rejoiced at the fall. Babylon inherited much of the empire under Nebuchadnezzar II. Nineveh was never rebuilt as a capital.
